scope: Client-side event block-execution state: what a 0x0130 RunEventFunction needs in order to run, what a 0x0131 EndEvent actually tears down, and the shared event-command queue both are submitted through. Opened against a live defect where ending an event server-side while a client-function call is outstanding leaves the client unable to render any later event until relog.
method: Read-only headless Ghidra via tools/ghidra/run-headless.ps1: DumpFunctionDecomp.java, DumpFunctionListing.java, DumpMemRange.java, FindAllReferencesToAddress.java, FindSymbolByName.java.

Entered from the dispatch chain in manifests/event_dialog_subsystem.json; walked parser -> receiver ctor -> submit wrapper -> command queue -> per-frame drain -> receiver Apply -> event-context method -> event vtable.
Class identity from RTTI COL -> TypeDescriptor -> name string over 0x0117208C..0x011722F0 and 0x012D7700..0x012D7940.

eventCommandQueue.summary: 0x012F, 0x0130, 0x0131 and two sibling command classes all submit through one shared FIFO. Submission is not execution.
eventCommandQueue.queueLocator: *(*(luaActorImplSubObject + 0x220))->[+0x04]->[+0xF4]; the +0x220 hop is FUN_00CC7510 (thunk to FUN_00CD7910, 'return this + 0x220')

queueLayout.+0x10: pending count - the submit gate reads this

submitWrappers.sibling_b: FUN_0076C720, inlined variant of the same shape

eventCommandQueue.submitSemantics: if queue[+0x10] != 0, skip the inline attempt entirely; else run the per-class precheck and, on SUCCESS, FUN_00794250 = vtable[2] Receive then vtable[3] Apply. If the inline attempt did not complete, clone via vtable[1] (FUN_00794240) and push_back via FUN_00785570 -> FUN_007238B0. Read off the FUN_007859B0 listing, 0x007859E3..0x00785A7D.

prechecks.0x0130: FUN_0089E3F0 -> FUN_0089E320 - unpacks luaParams at packet+0x49 through StartServerOrderEventFunctionChecker::UnpackerFunctor (FUN_008A0870); SUCCESS only when the resulting pending-target vector is empty

drain.calledFrom: FUN_00578970 LuaFrameTick (BCS-Y-1701) <- FUN_004DA680 Application_FrameTick (BCS-Y-1711), every frame
drain.semantics: pop-front loop running FUN_00794250 per head command. Status DAT_012C3120 (Receive failed) BREAKS the loop and leaves the command at the head. Completed commands are destroyed, capped at 0x20 per frame.
drain.consequence: head-of-line blocking: a head command whose Receive never succeeds wedges every later event command, and a non-empty queue means no command is attempted inline.

eventExecutionContext.evidence: every EndEvent / RunEventFunction entry thunk does MOV ECX,[ECX+0xF8] before tail-calling the 0x0089xxxx implementation: FUN_006E1080, FUN_006E10A0, FUN_006E10C0, FUN_006E10E0, FUN_006E1140

fields.+0x08: client-side block-event slot, ExecutionClientSideBlockEvent* - the slot RunEventFunction resumes
fields.+0x0C: server-order block-event slot, ExecutionClientSideBlockEvent* - the slot whose start path emits the c2s EventStart
fields.+0x1E: the KickReceiver Branch-A inhibitor byte read by FUN_006E11D0; written by FUN_008947C0 (callers FUN_00703F60, FUN_006F94D0)

kickTargetState.+0x128: active/previous kick target actor id; when +0x12C is NO_ACTOR and this field is non-NO_ACTOR, KickReceiver follows its Branch-B2 target-check path
kickTargetState.+0x12C: staged/current kick target actor id; when non-NO_ACTOR, KickReceiver follows Branch A
kickTargetState.branchSummary: KickReceiver slot 2 tests [+0x12C] first. With an established current target it resolves that id and gates on actor[+0x5C] plus FUN_006E11D0. With no current target it tests [+0x128]; a previous target uses Branch B2 and the same +0x5C gate, while a cleared pair takes Branch B1 and stores a primary target only when receiver[+0x80] is set.

eventStart.semantics: allocates a 0x2C-byte ExecutionClientSideBlockEvent (FUN_00896680), deletes whatever held the target slot, installs it. Mode DAT_012D7C40 targets ctx+0x08 and arms locally via FUN_008962C0; mode DAT_012D7C41 targets ctx+0x0C and emits the c2s EventStart through FUN_0075E3A0 / FUN_0075E510 (BCS-Y-0429 / BCS-Y-0430).

fields.+0x1D: abort-notified-once latch, set by FUN_00893520 / FUN_008935B0 / FUN_00893800
fields.+0x20: 'a server order has already executed against this event' - set to 1 by FUN_00896F70 on the successful RunEventFunction path
fields.+0x21: armed flag - set by FUN_008962C0, cleared by FUN_00893C80 / FUN_00893D00
fields.+0x24: unpacked-order payload pointer used by FUN_00896950
fields.+0x28: ClientOrderEventWaitingResumeChecker* - non-null exactly while the Lua event coroutine is suspended awaiting a server client-order

vtableSlots.3 (+0x0C): FUN_00892670 - 'return 0'. Hard false; this is the predicate the name-matched EndEvent handlers test before freeing the event.
vtableSlots.4 (+0x10): FUN_00892680 - 'return this[+0x28] != 0'. The RunEventFunction execution gate.
vtableSlots.5 (+0x14): FUN_00893160 - allocates a 12-byte ClientOrderEventWaitingResumeChecker via FUN_00899490
vtableSlots.7 (+0x1C): FUN_008926A0 - canceller: if this[+0x28] != 0 then checker[+0x08]=1, checker[+0x09]=arg, checker[+0x04]=0, this[+0x28]=0
vtableSlots.8 (+0x20): FUN_00896950 - runs the unpacked server order via FUN_008962C0

executionClientSideBlockEvent.slotAttributionEvidence: FindAllReferencesToAddress on 0x00892670 / 0x00892680 / 0x00892690 / 0x008926A0 returns exactly one DATA reference each, at 0x0105708C / 0x01057090 / 0x01057098 / 0x0105709C - all inside this vftable and nowhere else.

clientOrderEventWaitingResumeChecker.role: the object the Lua VM polls to decide whether a suspended event coroutine may resume; its presence in ExecutionClientSideBlockEvent+0x28 is the 'client-function call in flight' state

runEventFunction_0x0130.receiveSlot2: FUN_0089EB20 -> FUN_0089E8E0, draining the receiver's pending-target vector at +0xCC. The ctor zeroes that vector, so a freshly parsed packet returns SUCCESS immediately.

executionGate.condition: actor resolvable (FUN_00CC7190 or FUN_00CC7A50) AND actor[+0x5C] != 0 AND ctx[+0x08] != NULL AND ctx[+0x08]->vtable[4]() != 0
executionGate.vtable4Meaning: ExecutionClientSideBlockEvent+0x28 != 0 - the client's event coroutine is suspended awaiting a server client-order
executionGate.onPass: sets ctx[+0x08][+0x20] = 1, then FUN_00896950 -> FUN_008962C0 resumes the coroutine with the packet's functionName and luaParams and re-arms the event (+0x21 = 1)
executionGate.onFail: falls through to FUN_00894090 -> FUN_0075E670, which sends c2s opcode 0x012E at size 0x68 through FUN_004D6D30

pendingTargetResolution.vector: receiver sub-object at +0xCC; entries are 8 bytes each
pendingTargetResolution.phase1: Forward scan calls FUN_00CC7A50, then FUN_00CC7180, then FUN_00CC78C0 for each entry; the tracked source leaves the third call's semantic role unresolved.
pendingTargetResolution.phase3: Backwards scan calls FUN_00CC7A50 and checks FUN_00CC72A0 before shifting one 8-byte entry and decrementing the vector end, so dispatch drains from the back (LIFO).
pendingTargetResolution.result: An empty vector returns the success byte; unresolved entries leave the vector non-empty and return the failure byte, allowing the event command to remain pending.

packetLayoutAsClientReadsIt.+0x04: u8 teardown-variant selector, stored raw into receiver+0x0C by FUN_0078DDA0 (bare byte store, no validation)
packetLayoutAsClientReadsIt.+0x08: u8 event type, stored raw into receiver+0x0D by FUN_0078DE00

endEvent_0x0131.layoutNote: The client consumes only one byte at +0x04, so a sender using that layout feeds an actor-id low byte into the teardown-variant selector.
endEvent_0x0131.receiveSlot2: FUN_0089D200 - unconditional SUCCESS writer, so an EndEvent never wedges the queue

dispatchStage1.tables: byte table at 0x008A149C (102 entries), dword table at 0x008A1464 (14 entries)

bands.0..5: invoke - all six slots are the identical body 'MOV ECX,[EAX+0x18]; JMP FUN_008A09E0'

dispatchStage2.key: *(byte*)(receiver + 0x0C) = packet+0x04 selector byte; anything above 5 falls to a bare RET

teardownVariants.actions: ctx[+0x08]->vtable[7](0) cancels the pending call (+0x28 = 0, checker resumed with result 0); +0x1C latch, then vtable[2] = FUN_00893D00 closes the scene; then tests vtable[3]
teardownVariants.whyNot: the free is gated on vtable[3] = FUN_00892670, a hard 'return 0'. ctx[+0x08] is left non-null on a dead event with +0x28 == 0.

teardownVariants.actions: as selector 0 but cancels with arg 1 and latches +0x1D

deletes and nulls ctx[+0x0C] and clears ctx[+0x1C] / [+0x1D]. For ctx[+0x08]: if [+0x20] == 1 it clears [+0x22] and notifies only; otherwise it notifies and, when FUN_00CD0980() != 1, deletes the event and sets ctx[+0x08] = 0.
teardownVariants.note: the only variant that can free the client-side block-event slot, and the only one that does not require the event name to match

confirmedFromBinary: Pending-call state and scene teardown are separate: EndEvent selectors 0 and 1 cancel ExecutionClientSideBlockEvent+0x28 and run the scene-close path, but can never free ctx[+0x08], because the free is gated on a vtable slot that hard-returns 0.

A 0x0130 runs only when ctx[+0x08] is non-null AND ctx[+0x08][+0x28] is non-null. After a selector-0 or selector-1 EndEvent, +0x28 is 0, so a later 0x0130 fails the gate and never invokes its Lua function.
The event execution context lives at actor+0xF8, not on the zone, which matches zone changes not clearing the condition.
The c2s EventStart emit chain (BCS-Y-0426..0431) never touches actor+0xF8, which is why input, targeting and event-start emission keep working while event execution does not.
notConfirmed: Whether the second 0x0130 dies at the FUN_00896F70 gate or earlier at the command-queue gate (queue[+0x10] != 0). Both are live drop sites.
Whether the Lua event script re-enters FUN_00897310 on a later click, which would reinstall ctx[+0x08] and mask the stale slot.
The call site that installs the checker into +0x28; vtable slot 6 is only reachable through an indexed virtual call.
defectModel.discriminator: FUN_00896F70's failure branch sends c2s opcode 0x012E at size 0x68. A 104-byte 0x012E arriving shortly after an ignored 0x0130 puts the drop at the FUN_00896F70 gate; nothing arriving puts it upstream, at the command-queue gate.

serverRecommendation.primary: EndEvent +0x04 is a one-byte teardown-variant selector, not an actor id. Selector 5 routes to FUN_00893800, the only variant that unconditionally frees ctx[+0x0C], can free ctx[+0x08], and does not require the event name to match.
serverRecommendation.caveat: FUN_00893800 skips the ctx[+0x08] free when that event's +0x20 is 1, which FUN_00896F70 sets on every successful RunEventFunction. For an event that already rendered a client-function call, selector 5 frees ctx[+0x0C] but may leave ctx[+0x08] installed.
serverRecommendation.fallbackIfNoEscape: if selector 5 does not clear the condition in practice, no server-sendable escape exists for the post-render case, and the server should refuse to end an event with a client-function call in flight rather than releasing the player into a broken state.
